clue.text: Old chairman's unusual means of making notes

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of old chairman are to be set out in an unexpected new order

parts.note: the possessive 's is no letter, so the word gives its own eight letters

explanation.surface: An elderly chairman has an odd way of taking notes at meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means of making notes' suggests jotting minutes, but the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is played by blowing through reeds to produce musical tones.

clue.text: Work fellow's acquired could be "Great Expectations"

indicators.note: one piece acquiring another takes it inside

parts.note: fellow's read as fellow has gives he's
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A colleague's purchase might be a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Fellow's is read as 'he has', HE'S, which acquires the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Great expectations are high aspirations, and the plural fits wishes.

clue.text: Go downhill in syndicate for, gambling

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ring is a group working together, a syndicate
to ski is to go downhill on skis

explanation.surface: Joining a ski syndicate as a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Risking money on a chance outcome is betting it.

clue.text: It's readily available when in difficulty

definitions.meaning: present and at hand right there
put in an awkward position, pressed to respond

explanation.surface: Something is handy whenever trouble strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both immediately present and placed in a tough situation.

clue.text: Elected and showing variation in objective

parts.note: a politician who is elected is in
things showing variation are different

explanation.surface: A candidate voted in and differing in aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a noun, a goal, but it is the adjective meaning impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impartial and without bias is unconcerned with any outcome.

clue.text: A foot behind

explanation.surface: Someone is a foot to the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical term for towards the stern, at the rear.

clue.text: Small amount in gratuity rejected by singer

annotationWithheld.why: Small amount in gratuity rejected by singer (5): PIPIT reversed is TIPIP, TIP round PI, but PI is no recognised small amount; the piece the wordplay needs is unclear
annotationWithheld.clue: Small amount in gratuity rejected by singer

clue.text: Managed to get doctor round after climbing accident

indicators.note: round places one piece around the other
in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner
to run a business is to manage it, so managed is ran

explanation.surface: A medic arrived after a mountaineering mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, especially of a car or aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is a minor crash or collision.

clue.text: Pirates' pieces of coin

indicators.note: breaking into pieces tells us to rearrange the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Buccaneers' pieces of eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces of coin' reads as pirate loot, but 'pieces of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A piastre is a monetary unit of Egypt and other Middle Eastern countries.

clue.text: Borne with real trouble when carried outside

indicators.note: carried outside means the carrying word goes around the other

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so the word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Real trouble was endured when brought outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put up with has been endured.

clue.text: Sat to entertain appeal as put forward

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed
IT is informal for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone sat and invited an attractive proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit an idea is to propose it as a basis for argument.

clue.text: State intervention in wake of distress

indicators.note: an intervention comes between parties, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: the wake of a boat is the trail it leaves behind
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Government steps in after a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' looks like part of the phrase 'in wake of distress', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful toil or suffering, a state of anguish.

clue.text: First sign of simian with long backbone

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: An ape with a long spine is a sign of evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal column is the backbone of a vertebrate.

clue.text: Soldiers carried by aircraft and boat

indicators.note: one piece carried by another sits inside it

parts.note: a fighter is a type of military aircraft
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops are moved by plane and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship built to carry cargo.

clue.text: Removal of race under about one mile

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed after
about means turning around, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nation is a race of people

explanation.surface: A race is moved to under a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing I + MILE gives ELIMI, with NATION placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elimination is getting rid of something, taking it away.

clue.text: Search for accommodation is not concluded

indicators.note: a word not concluded loses its final letter

parts.note: DIGS is British informal for rented lodgings

explanation.surface: A hunt for lodgings goes on without end.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGS is British slang for a rented room.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig for something is to search for it.

clue.text: Leave I have needed when working badly

parts.note: to defect is to leave one's country or side
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Time off was needed when performing poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Defective means faulty, not functioning properly.

clue.text: The last word in divine jam

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to divine the future is to predict it
AMEN is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

explanation.surface: The final say on a heavenly preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine jam' reads as a delicious preserve; 'divine' is a verb and 'jam' means a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is a tight spot, an awkward situation.

clue.text: Crazed gorilla almost ate reptile

indicators.note: crazed suggests madness, so the letters are scrambled
almost means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A frenzied gorilla nearly devoured a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodile-like reptile of the Americas and China.

clue.text: Charge by police should suit the case

parts.note: to charge a glass or pipe is to fill it
THE BILL is British slang for the police (also a long-running TV police drama)

explanation.surface: A police accusation ought to fit the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BILL is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill the bill is to be exactly what is required.

clue.text: Descent by rope taking a long time

parts.note: a line is a rope or cord
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A slow descent by rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests abseiling, but it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, the line of descent from forebears.

clue.text: Bananas mother sent back

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the word backwards

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Mum returns some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Horse with new energy makes its name

definitions.text: Horse with new energy makes its name

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
GO is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A revitalised horse becomes famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Marengo was Napoleon's famous grey war horse, named after his 1800 victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's grey charger bore this name, taken from his famous battle.

clue.text: Working group in intelligence agency for business associations

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a machine that is on is working
a sort is a kind or group

explanation.surface: A task force within the spy service serves business groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are groups of companies combined for a joint venture.

clue.text: Public exhibition in Dover throughout the year

indicators.note: an exhibition puts something on display, here a word on show within the clue's words

explanation.surface: A show in Dover runs all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not concealed.

clue.text: Show embarrassment when injured in the ring, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to blush or turn red in the face
wounded by a bull's horns in the bullring

explanation.surface: Someone blushes after being hurt in a bullfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests boxing, but it is the bullring, where a matador may be horned.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador pierced by a bull's horns has been tossed and wounded; reddening the face shows shame.

clue.text: Compulsion to drop University garb

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: duress is compulsion by threats

explanation.surface: Being forced to give up academic gowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, a manner of attire.

clue.text: Lines written on a person's character in descriptive language

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a person's image is the public character they present
RY, railway, gives lines

explanation.surface: Lines are written about someone's personality in vivid prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is vivid figurative wording that creates pictures in the mind.

clue.text: Utterance from young boxer, say, put up to settle score

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to settle a score or bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A young fighter's remark about paying back an old grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter; it is the dog breed, whose puppy gives a sharp bark.
explanation.definitionFit: A yap is a shrill bark, typical of a small or young dog.

clue.text: After a smash, tennis elbow's beginning to become acute

indicators.note: after a smash the word is broken and its letters reassembled differently
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Tennis elbow becomes severe after a hard shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash' is a tennis shot here, but it signals that the letters of TENNIS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense pain is acute, felt very strongly.

clue.text: Competition that's fair and square

parts.note: a fair contest is even
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can mean square

explanation.surface: A contest that is fair and above board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair and square' is an idiom, but here each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a contest in a sports programme.

clue.text: Poor writer going to unfair ends to meet debts

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: IOUs are written promises of debts

explanation.surface: A struggling author resorts to dishonest means to pay off loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Penurious means extremely poor, living in want.
